messages:
mira: quick follow-up to the RFC — i sketched a lightweight 'probe-adjudicator' component that lives outside the router and makes soft-eviction decisions for canary/A-B traffic. goal: reduce blast radius while keeping fast warmups and minimal traffic oscillation.
kevin: couple quick q's — why decouple from the router instead of embedding logic? cost/complexity tradeoff?
alex: fwiw i like decoupling. router stays simple stateless, adjudicator can be stateful and maintain rolling windows + model of tenant baselines. also lets us reuse for Dedicated/private.
mira: exactly. adjudicator responsibilities: ingest per-route probes, compute signal fusion (errors + p95 + regressions vs baseline), emit directed actions (reduce pct, steer to fallback, soft-evict X%). router subscribes to actions and applies them atomically.
sam: soft-evict semantics? is that immediate removal or gradual? we should avoid oscillation when signals are noisy.
mira: soft-evict = temporary attenuate variant's share by N% for a cooldown window, not full kill. rejoin requires passing a targeted probe (small controlled traffic) and sustained healthy stats for a rejoin window.
julia: can we see a sample config? helps me think about consoling and runbooks.
mira: pasted a minimal rollout config below (proposal):
```yaml
rollout:
  id: ab_v83
  variant: b
  initial_traffic_pct: 5
  probe_window_s: 120
  signals:
    - name: error_rate
      threshold: 0.015
    - name: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 750
  soft_eviction:
    eviction_pct: 40 # percent of variant traffic to remove when triggered
    cooldown_s: 300
    rejoin_policy: probe-first
    probe_size_pct: 1
```
kevin: ok nice. how do we prevent cascading re-evictions in multi-tenant bursts? if many adjudicators emit actions, router could thrash.
alex: router should batch actions and apply smoothing (exponential moving avg) + global cap on total simultaneous eviction. also adjudicator can include confidence score; low-confidence actions are advisory only.
mira: yes — confidence + action_ttl. we also want a global circuit-breaker tier that can veto per-route actions during infra-wide incidents.
ops: what about metrics and alerts? want precise signals to avoid noisy ops pages.
mira: agreed. propose these telemetry outputs:
- adjudicator.decisions.count (action_type, reason, confidence)
- adjudicator.probe.results (route, variant, success, latency_ms)
- router.applied.actions (route, before_pct, after_pct, applied_by)
- variant.traffic.proportions (time series per-tenant)
- rollback.events (manual/auto, trigger_reason)
ops: add an alert for repeated soft-eviction > 3 times in 1h for same variant -> page.
sam: edge case: what if soft-eviction reduces variant below probe size -> it never gets probed and stays evicted. we need rejoin scheduling independent of traffic share.
mira: good catch. plan: adjudicator maintains a scheduled rejoin probe that ignores current traffic allocation (sends synthetic probes or bootstraps probes through a mirror path). probe-first rejoin means we send 1% synthetic or mirrored requests to the variant for evaluation.
julia: security/compliance question: private deployments need to avoid sending real requests to adjudicator service (if hosted). mind on-prem flow?
alex: adjudicator can be deployed as a local sidecar or tenant-scoped instance in Private mode. control plane APIs are identical but the adjudicator endpoint can be internal-only.
mira: on rollout safety: default policy for critical routes = disable soft-eviction (only hard rollback via operator). non-critical routes use soft-eviction. we'll expose granular policy flags in the rollout config.
kevin: implementation quick sketch? thoughts on storage for rolling windows?
mira: use a time-series summarizer per-route (count, errors, lat buckets) in Redis streams or a small TSDB. adjudicator ingests aggregates, not raw traces. decision loop runs every 30s per-route.
julia: can we add a small governance UI to outline current soft-eviction state per-tenant? product wants to see 'why I lost traffic'.
mira: yes — router/applied.actions stream powers console view with reasons + confidence. we'll add a 'request appeal' button for operators to force re-eval.
sam: rollout playbook note: when a variant is soft-evicted, we should automatically open a short-lived canary-only debug trace collection mode to capture deterministic failures.
mira: great idea. add to runbook.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: ab_v83 canary rollout started by @mira at 1765433300, variant b @ 5% traffic. check /deploys/ab_v83 for status.
kevin: cool. final: i'll write the adjudicator proto + minimal router subscribe API. follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30am. :thumbsup:
mira: thanks all — i'll update the RFC with the config snippet, telemetry list, and runbook notes. agenda: land proto PR, quick PoC, and console mock for appeal flow. :eyes:
